read_extent.submission: All five physical pages including committee cover, full financing recommendation and full seaport example.
read_extent.primary_law: Entire one-page BFinHBRuaG including sections 1–3 and version note, last amended 2017.
read_extent.addressed_draft: Original BR780/25 cover and complete opening problem, solution, budget-effects and costs sections; not the whole long bill.

assessment: The matching 38.4 mantissa, annual subsidy wording and coastal-Länder infrastructure context identify the statutory EUR38.346 million grant. Billion is approximately one thousand times too large. A broader maritime-spending interpretation does not readily explain this exact match, but the correction should remain confined to the identifiable grant.
materiality: Minor: auxiliary illustration without a derived financing total or decisive threshold; the broader maintenance-financing recommendation survives. A clerical million/billion substitution is a strong alternative explanation.
direction: True only for the explicit claim that replacing this ordinary annual baseline with SVIK borrowing frees money for social expenditure. It enlarges that claimed room for substitution. Direction for every broader tax/fee-financing request is not separately proved.
limits: No conclusion that actual diversion occurs, that federal total port-related spending is only the statutory grant, or that the broad infrastructure-financing concern is unfounded.
The exact addressed BR version is expressly named in the author body; the later committee cover associates BT21/4099. This review does not assume complete identity of the two versions.
